# HANDOFF: Sentry — everything still to do

Written 2026-09-04 after a full audit of both repos. Read this end to end
before touching anything. Every claim below has file:line evidence; where I
could not verify something from code I have said so explicitly and marked it
VERIFY FIRST. Do not skip those.

---

## 0. THE ONE-PARAGRAPH SUMMARY

Sentry is installed in both repos, has ~2,900 call sites, and until today the
World Hub browser reported **nothing at all** — three capture sites were
guarded on `window.Sentry`, a global that `@sentry/nextjs` v8+ does not define
and that nothing in either repo assigns. `beforeSend` additionally discarded
every `ReferenceError`, which is the exact class minified bundles throw. A test
named `sentry-coverage` was green through all of it, because it greps seven
files for substrings. PR #1316 fixed the dead capture sites and made that test
assert something real. **What remains is mostly delivery, not capture**: no
source maps anywhere, no release tagging on the Hub, zero cron monitors against
~58 scheduled jobs, and an engine whose excellent instrumentation may be
pointed at no DSN.

## 1. ENVIRONMENT — read before your first command

You are probably on Dan's Mac in a Cowork session.

- **`node` is NOT on the default PATH.** Prefix everything:
  `export PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/$(ls ~/.nvm/versions/node | tail -1)/bin:$PATH"`
- **Never work in the main clones.** `~/Documents/Smarter-Poker-World-Hub` and
  `~/Documents/Smarter-Poker-Club-Arena` are other agents' dirty worktrees.
  Claim your own: `git worktree add -b <branch> ~/Documents/.agent-trees/<repo>/<name> origin/main`
- **The pre-push hook takes ~3 minutes** (guards, tsc, then the tests covering
  your diff). Launch with `nohup git push > /tmp/push.log 2>&1 & disown` and
  poll. **Never `--no-verify`.**
- **`gh` is not authenticated** (`HTTP 401: Bad credentials`). Use the GitHub
  MCP tools for PRs and issues.
- **You do NOT have the `workflow` token permission.** Any change to a file
  under `.github/workflows/` will be rejected. Two items below need it — they
  are marked WORKFLOW PERMISSION REQUIRED and must go to Dan or to an agent
  with a wider token.
- **Push, open the PR, report the number, stop.** Autopilot merges. Do not sit
  in a loop watching CI (CLAUDE.md 10.8.3).

## 3. WORK ITEMS, IN PRIORITY ORDER

### P1 — #1317: Sentry cannot tell us a job STOPPED RUNNING

**The single most valuable thing on this list.** Zero cron monitors exist:
`grep -rn "captureCheckIn\|monitorSlug\|withMonitor"` across both repos returns
no matches. Against 17 `vercel.json` crons, 32 `pages/api/cron/` handlers (only
10 of which import `reportApiError`), and ~58 Open Claw jobs.

Sentry today reports that a job which *ran* threw. It can never report that a
job **stopped**. Two incidents this week were exactly that shape: the workers
hop 401'd for a full day (2026-08-31), and a doubled engine hand rate ran 53
hours until a **Supabase billing email** surfaced it.

**Do:**
1. Wrap `fire_cron` in `scripts/openclaw-cron-dispatcher.py` — one place,
   covers all ~58 jobs. `in_progress` before the HTTP call, `ok`/`error` after,
   slug derived from the job name.
2. Wrap the Vercel handlers via the shared route wrapper with
   `Sentry.withMonitor(slug, fn, { schedule })`, so the 22 console-only
   handlers are covered without editing each.
3. Derive each monitor's schedule and grace period from the cron expression
   already in the dispatcher, so the two cannot drift.
4. Start with the jobs whose silence costs most: `sp_prune_hand_history_10m`,
   `sp_prune_hand_state_snapshots_2m` (if these stop, the disk fills — see §5),
   the horse social/story jobs, `auth-integrity-audit`.

**Trap:** deploying the dispatcher requires `bash scripts/deploy-openclaw.sh`.
The repo file and the Hetzner file must never drift (CLAUDE.md 11.3). That
script was silently broken for months because it referenced an SSH key that was
never created — confirm it actually succeeds, do not assume.

**Verify:** watch one full fire-cycle in production and confirm the check-in
appears in Sentry. A monitor you cannot see check in is the same bug one level
up.

### P2 — Club Arena #2917: the engine may be reporting to nothing

**VERIFY FIRST — this issue's premise may already be false.**

`server/src/services/errorReporter.ts` is the best Sentry code in either repo:
713 call sites across 92 files, non-`Error` coercion, uncaught/unhandled
integrations, flush-on-shutdown, and incident-informed **rate limiting** rather
than blanket filtering (`:69-77` records that the old blanket filter is what hid
the 2026-08-15 table freeze).

If `SENTRY_DSN` is unset, `errorReporter.ts:48` warns and all 713 call sites
become console writes. `server/output.log` lines 6, 1383 and 1397 show three
boots doing exactly that.

`auto-deploy-hetzner.yml:429-430` checks for the variable and prints
`WARN … non-blocking`, then deploys. **Four lines above**, an empty
`server/.env` refuses to deploy, reasoning *"worse than not deploying, because
it looks alive."* The same argument applies here and was not made.

**Do:**
1. `grep '^SENTRY_DSN=..' <repo>/server/.env` on the Hetzner host. If present
   and events are flowing, close the issue and do only step 2.
2. Make the check blocking, matching the `.env` gate above it.
   **WORKFLOW PERMISSION REQUIRED.**
3. Consider a boot assertion in `GameServer.ts` beside `initSentry()` at `:549`
   so the engine refuses to start in production with no reporting path. This
   needs no workflow permission and is the more robust half.

### P3 — #1318: every stack trace is minified

**World Hub.** `withSentryConfig` is imported (`next.config.js:77`) and its two
option objects built (`:1057-1071`, `:1074-1098`) — and `:1113-1114` exports
`withPWA(nextConfig)` only. Both objects are dead variables. No source maps, no
debug IDs, no release. The disabling is a **documented OOM workaround**
(`:1100-1112`), so this is not a flip — measure a real build. The
auto-instrumentation is the memory-hungry part; `sourcemaps.disable: false`
with auto-instrumentation left off is the likely shape, but prove it.

**Club Arena.** `vite.config.ts:57` gates the plugin on
`NODE_ENV === 'production' && SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`. `ci.yml:1120-1140` sets all
four — but that build is a CI check whose artifact does not ship.
`publish-club-arena.yml:346-355`, which builds the production bundle, omits
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`. **WORKFLOW PERMISSION REQUIRED.**

Verified against the shipped artifact, not inferred: **837** `.js` files carry
`//# sourceMappingURL=`, **0** `.map` files exist, **0** files carry an injected
Sentry `debugId`.

**The release names do not match, so the token alone will not fix it:**
runtime is `club-arena@${VITE_APP_VERSION}` (`SentryInit.ts:99`) and
`publish-club-arena.yml:354` sets that to the **git SHA**; the plugin uses
`club-arena@${npm_package_version}` (`vite.config.ts:74`). Make both derive
from one value.

**Also:** `.env.example:34-35` still carries the known-bad `smarter-poker` /
`club-arena` org and project slugs that `vite.config.ts:53-56` documents as
404ing and silently no-opping uploads. And `.env.example:63` says
`SENTRY_TOKEN` while `next.config.js:1067` reads `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` — anyone
following the example sets the wrong name.

### P5 — AUDIT (dashboard, not code): is anything actually arriving?

**Everything above is unverifiable from the repo.** You must check the Sentry
dashboard and Vercel env vars. Nobody has confirmed these:

1. **Is `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` / `SENTRY_DSN` set in Vercel at all?** It is in
   no committed file, no `vercel.json`, and no workflow. If it is unset, every
   `captureException` in the Hub is a silent no-op and PR #1316 changed nothing
   in practice. **Check this before doing any other work on this list.**
2. **Are there any alert rules?** Events arriving with nobody notified is the
   same failure as no events. Expect none to exist.
3. **Event volume per project, last 30 days.** If the Hub project shows ~0
   browser events, that confirms (1) from the other side.
4. **Quota and rate limits.** `.agent/audits/2026-08-12-...md:106` records a
   **413** from the Sentry ingest endpoint — something was already sending
   payloads too large. Find out what.
5. **Are Hub and Arena separate projects?** `next.config.js:677-692` has a CSP
   report-only entry for `o4510810580779008.ingest.us.sentry.io` — but that
   traffic is explainable by the Arena SPA on the same origin, so it does not
   prove the Hub has its own DSN.
6. **PII.** `IdentityDNA.ts:206` calls `setSentryUser` on login. Confirm what
   fields go up and whether `sendDefaultPii` is off.

### P6 — Arena client gaps (real, none filed yet)

1. **Lazy init loses early crashes.** `SentryInit.ts:220-234` defers the SDK
   load to `requestIdleCallback(..., {timeout:3000})` or `setTimeout(...,100)`.
   Until it resolves, Sentry's **global handlers are not installed**, so any
   uncaught exception or unhandled rejection in that window is lost entirely.
   Wrapper calls queue (max 50, `:32`); raw crashes do not. Early-boot crashes
   are the ones that matter most and the ones least likely to be caught. Fix:
   install lightweight `window.onerror` / `unhandledrejection` listeners
   synchronously that buffer into the existing queue.
2. **Chunk failures are invisible.** `ErrorBoundary.tsx:43-82` returns at `:81`
   before reaching Sentry for `ChunkLoadError` / `Failed to fetch` /
   `dynamically imported module` / `Unable to preload CSS`. Deliberate, but it
   means a **bad deploy** — the case where these spike — shows nothing. At
   minimum count them; ideally sample.
3. **`beforeSend` `:160-163`** drops `Cannot read properties of null` unless the
   stack contains `/src/`. After minification stacks rarely contain `/src/`, so
   with no source maps (P3) this likely drops real null-derefs. Revisit once
   source maps land — the two are coupled.
4. **`beforeSendTransaction` `:176-182`** drops every transaction under 100ms.
   Fine for noise, but it also hides "suspiciously fast" regressions.
5. **`startTransaction` `:326-332`** returns `undefined` when Sentry has not
   loaded and is not queued — early performance spans vanish silently.

### P7 — Coverage: 73% of World Hub catch blocks report nothing

**2,031** `catch` blocks under `pages/api/`; **541** `reportApiError` call sites
across 513 of 632 route files. So roughly **27%** report. The other ~1,490 are
`console.error` only (2,898 such calls).

Worst concentration: **22 of 32** `pages/api/cron/` handlers do not import
`reportApiError` at all.

Do not attempt a bulk sweep — it will be a 1,500-file diff nobody can review.
Do the 22 cron handlers first (they overlap P1 and are the least observable
surface), then triage the rest by blast radius: money paths, auth, seating.

Arena is fine here and needs no work: engine 713 reports vs 534 catches; client
1,522 vs 1,626.

### P8 — Enhancements worth doing once the basics work

- **Release health.** No `release` in any of the Hub's three `Sentry.init`
  calls and no `SENTRY_RELEASE`, so every event lands on "no release" — no
  regression attribution, no "first seen in". `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` is
  already available. Do this alongside P3 or it will be forgotten.
- **A synthetic smoke test.** All three Hub configs set
  `enabled: NODE_ENV === 'production'`, so the wiring is **never exercised
  before it ships**. That is why three dead capture sites survived. Add a
  deploy-time step that throws a tagged test error and asserts it appears via
  the Sentry API. This is the check that would have caught the whole class.
- **Dual init.** `vendor/commander-shared/src/lib/commander/errorMonitoring.js:15`
  is a **second** `Sentry.init` for Commander. Confirm it does not fight the
  Next.js SDK's client — two inits in one page is usually a bug.
- **Tracing.** Review `tracesSampleRate` on both apps. Not audited; unknown.

## 4. TRAPS

1. **`window.Sentry` does not exist and never will.** If you find yourself
   writing `if (window.Sentry)`, you are writing a no-op. Import the SDK.
   `sentry-coverage.test.mjs` now fails the build on this.
2. **A green `sentry-coverage` never meant Sentry worked.** It grepped seven
   files for substrings and passed with the whole client blind. Believe the
   dashboard, not the test.
3. **Filtering by error CLASS throws the bugs away with the noise.** The old
   config dropped every ReferenceError to avoid stale-chunk spam. Filter the
   known identifiers by NAME.
4. **CI builds are not shipping builds.** Arena's `ci.yml` feeds the source-map
   plugin correctly; `publish-club-arena.yml` is what players get, and it does
   not. Always ask which workflow produces the artifact.
5. **A `WARN … non-blocking` on a reporting path is a decision to be blind.**
   See P2, and note the gate four lines above it makes the opposite call.
6. **Do not add a `schedule:` trigger to a GitHub workflow.** CLAUDE.md §11
   routes scheduled application work through Open Claw and CI enforces it.
